intro:
Escaping from Zilah (Zalau)

April 16, 1919

Comrade Commisar, the situation is dangerous. After our new, revolutionary government refused to retreat behind the new demarcation lines, the imperialist hyenas insited their capitalist lapdogs, the Romanian and the so called "Czechoslovakian" reactionists. They mobilized their armies and attacked our weak, inexperienced troops. Your job is securing the railway station at NagykÃ¡roly as long as possible to cover our retreat.

ORDER: Hold at least one VH, keep your MSU alive and move it onto the Escape Hex at NagykÃ¡roly.

NOTES:
- AI moves first.
- The longer you hold on, the better result you get.
- You have 3 free RTP slots.

12 Turns

Scenario designed by Csaba (lvjtn)

lose.text: The front has collapsed. The Republic has lost the army and time it needed; hostile forces advance while counterrevolutionary detachments prepare their reprisals.

briefing.act: ACT I — THE EASTERN FRONT BREAKS

dialogue.speaker: András Fekete
dialogue.text: Don't use the station clock; it's stopped at six. The Zilah trains are arriving without schedules, with wounded men and guns whose teams we've lost. I need the sidings cleared. You can already hear Romanian artillery beyond them.

dialogue.speaker: Béla Kun
dialogue.role: People's Commissar for Foreign Affairs — Field Telephone
dialogue.text: Böhm, I need that railway kept open. Károlyi resigned over the new demarcation line; we inherited his empty depots, and now the Romanians are forcing us west. Paris is waiting to see whether this government can keep an army.

dialogue.speaker: Vilmos Böhm
dialogue.text: Look at the battalions on that line. Some have no artillery, and the villages are receiving orders from three headquarters. The Romanians crossed at dawn. Give me time to get the army onto the trains; I cannot stop them here.

dialogue.speaker: Vilmos Böhm
dialogue.role: Social Democrat and People's Commissar for Military Affairs
dialogue.text: The officers loading those trains talk about defending Hungary. So do most of the soldiers. If you ask them to fight only for world revolution, Kun, you'll lose men we need. They have to believe we're defending their country too.

dialogue.speaker: Béla Kun
dialogue.text: And what happens when those officers are offered the old flag without the councils? We need them, Böhm, but they don't get to decide what the Republic is for. Commissar, settle the rear guard: hold Nagykároly station, or keep moving along the roads?

choices.text: Fortify the station and approaches. Every additional hour lets more men, guns, and rolling stock escape west.
choices.hint: Gain an entrenched infantry detachment and near-full core resupply, but forgo the prestige and reconnaissance experience of the mobile rear guard.

choices.text: Keep the rear guard mobile. Delay each enemy column, then withdraw before it closes the road behind us.
choices.hint: Gain a prestige award and experience for every core reconnaissance unit, but forgo the infantry detachment and near-full resupply.

dialogue.speaker: András Fekete
dialogue.text: I'll keep the locomotives under steam. Wounded men and guns go west first. Keep the cavalry off the sidings until the last train clears; after that I'll destroy the timetables we leave behind.

dialogue.speaker: Vilmos Böhm
dialogue.text: Give every commander a withdrawal road and an hour. I don't want a battalion staying in a village because it can't find the next headquarters. Once the rails are cut, we won't be able to get its guns out.

dialogue.speaker: Vilmos Böhm
dialogue.text: Headquarters goes to the western road. Keep infantry between the cavalry and the trains. Fekete, telephone me while you still have a line; I need to know what has got through.

orders.situation: Romanian and Czechoslovak forces have opened a general offensive against the weak eastern front. The Nagykároly railway is one of the last organised routes behind the threatened detachment.
orders.mission: Delay the enemy, protect the evacuation route, and withdraw the surviving command group before the encirclement closes.
primaryObjectives: Hold at least one victory objective
Move the MSU onto the escape hex at Nagykároly
secondaryObjectives: Preserve experienced units for the rebuilding of the Red Army
Delay the enemy without allowing the rear guard to be surrounded
orders.enemyIntelligence: The enemy moves first and has the initiative. Expect converging attacks against the railway and the routes leading west.
orders.availableSupport: Three free RTP slots are available. Railway personnel will assist the evacuation while the station remains in friendly hands.
orders.notes: 12 turns. The longer the delaying position survives, the better the result, but the MSU must still reach the escape hex.

intro:
Breaking through Nyíregyháza

April 24, 1919

Comrade Commisar, our troops weren't able to stop the overwhelmind Romanian attacks. We executed a few ex-KuK officers but it didn't help too much. We should retreat behind the Tisza River. You'd better hurry, two Romanian pincers are closing around Nyíregyháza.

ORDER: Hold at least one VH, keep your MSU alive and move it onto the Escape Hex at Tokaj.

NOTE: You have 3 free RTP slots.

16 Turns

Scenario designed by Csaba (lvjtn)

lose.text: The front has collapsed. The Republic has lost the army and time it needed; hostile forces advance while counterrevolutionary detachments prepare their reprisals.

briefing.act: ACT II — THE ROAD TO THE TISZA

dialogue.speaker: András Fekete
dialogue.text: The rear guard held beyond the planned departure hour. We used the extra time to clear the trains. I've brought the arrivals for the staff to check.

dialogue.speaker: András Fekete
dialogue.text: We got the formations out, but the line broke before all the transport cleared. I'll need replacements for the equipment left behind. The crews are already asking when.

dialogue.speaker: András Fekete
dialogue.text: The withdrawal was carried out in order. The formations are intact, which is more than the staff expected to be able to report.

dialogue.speaker: András Fekete
dialogue.text: More guns and wounded men reached us because you held the station. I can show Böhm the wagon returns if he still thinks we stayed too long.

dialogue.speaker: Vilmos Böhm
dialogue.text: You trusted my withdrawal times. The formations got out, but Fekete lost wagons he can't replace. I owe him an answer about those.

dialogue.speaker: András Fekete
dialogue.text: I have ammunition stacked at Nyíregyháza and no locomotive free to take it. The wounded are climbing onto wagons before they stop. Which headquarters controls the westbound traffic? I've been given three maps.

dialogue.speaker: Aurél Stromfeld
dialogue.text: Give me the maps. I'll issue one route order. Units are retreating separately and reporting to whichever telephone answers. We cannot hold all these towns, but we must keep Tokaj open until the formations cross the Tisza.

dialogue.speaker: Vilmos Böhm
dialogue.text: The men are tired and every abandoned wagon starts another betrayal story. They need an order we can carry out. Strike one Romanian pincer to reopen the road, or move the transport behind successive rear guards?

choices.text: Strike one pincer hard enough to reopen the road, then disengage before the second can arrive.
choices.hint: Gain a prestige award and experience for every core formation, but forgo full resupply and the additional transport column.

choices.text: Build successive rear-guard lines and move the transport first. The army must reach the Tisza intact.
choices.hint: Fully resupply every core formation and gain a transport column, but forgo the counterstroke's prestige and core-wide experience.

dialogue.speaker: Aurél Stromfeld
dialogue.text: Concentrate for a short attack. When the road opens, disengage. Put that in the battalion orders; I don't want anyone pursuing after we've got what we need.

dialogue.speaker: András Fekete
dialogue.text: I will send ammunition and wounded men toward Tokaj first. Once the last train leaves, the bridges and sidings can be denied to the enemy.

dialogue.speaker: Vilmos Böhm
dialogue.text: Get headquarters through Tokaj before the pincers meet. Keep officers with the guns and wagons. The men need to see that someone still knows where they're going.

orders.situation: The first defensive line has failed. Romanian columns are closing from more than one direction around Nyíregyháza, while the Tisza crossings remain the only defensible line to the west.
orders.mission: Break out of the threatened salient and withdraw the surviving force through Tokaj.
primaryObjectives: Hold at least one victory objective
Move the MSU onto the escape hex at Tokaj
secondaryObjectives: Keep the retreat corridor open for as long as possible
Evacuate valuable formations rather than fighting for ground that cannot be held
orders.enemyIntelligence: Two Romanian pincers are closing around Nyíregyháza. Their advance is rapid, but the spearheads may be vulnerable if attacked separately.
orders.availableSupport: Three free RTP slots are available. Remaining railway transport can accelerate the withdrawal while Tokaj is accessible.
orders.notes: 16 turns. Avoid a static last stand away from the escape route.

intro:
Szolnok: Securing The Bridgehead

May 1, 1919

Comrade Commisar, the Romanians have reached the Tisza, and a smaller vanguard has crossed the river at Szolnok. The retreat must end here and now, if the main troops of the reactionists can cross the Tisza, our proletarian state will collapse. Your job is to secure the western bank of the river and form a bridgehead on the eastern bank, if possible. But be cautious, more and more Romanian divisions are on their way.

ORDER: Hold at least 4 VHs and keep your MSU alive.

NOTES:
- You are awarded by an Ammunition Wagon (depot RTP) detachment.
- You can purchase two new units.
- You have 4 free RTP slots.

14 Turns

Scenario designed by Csaba (lvjtn)

lose.text: The front has collapsed. The Republic has lost the army and time it needed; hostile forces advance while counterrevolutionary detachments prepare their reprisals.

briefing.act: ACT III — THE LINE OF THE TISZA

dialogue.speaker: Béla Szántó
dialogue.text: The Romanians expected a rout and found a front. Budapest has stopped drafting evacuation orders.

dialogue.speaker: Béla Szántó
dialogue.text: We are on the Tisza because there was nowhere further to fall back to. The Council is asking questions this army cannot yet answer.

dialogue.speaker: Béla Szántó
dialogue.text: Budapest has been told we hold the Tisza. Before the Council announces anything more, I need to know whether the crossings are secure.

dialogue.speaker: Vilmos Böhm
dialogue.text: The rear guard held Hajduboszormeny to the last hour. The transport columns crossed the Tisza intact because of it.

dialogue.speaker: Vilmos Böhm
dialogue.text: Not one formation was lost in the withdrawal. The staff has been recalculating what this army can still be asked to do.

dialogue.speaker: Béla Szántó
dialogue.text: Budapest is celebrating May Day. I've been asked what news can be announced from this front. Romanian patrols are testing the bridges; I won't send reassurance until you tell me what is holding them.

dialogue.speaker: Vilmos Böhm
dialogue.text: A Romanian vanguard is already over near Szolnok. Engineers are preparing more crossings. We stop them here, or the road to Budapest is open. Which units can reach the western bank first?

dialogue.speaker: Aurél Stromfeld
dialogue.role: Chief of Staff, Hungarian Red Army
dialogue.text: First secure the western bank, the bridge and the depots. Then decide how much risk we take east of the river. Where does the mobile reserve wait: behind the crossings, or across them where it can seize the initiative before Romanian reinforcements arrive?

choices.text: Keep it west of the river to crush any breakthrough and protect the bridge and supply depots.
choices.hint: Gain an entrenched infantry detachment and a smaller prestige award, but forgo the larger prestige and core-wide experience of the eastern bridgehead.

choices.text: Send it across early and expand our own bridgehead before Romanian reinforcements arrive.
choices.hint: Gain a larger prestige award and experience for every core formation, but forgo the additional entrenched infantry detachment.

dialogue.speaker: Béla Szántó
dialogue.text: I'll support keeping the reserve west. But the Romanians mustn't put their guns on the far bank undisturbed. Prepare a counterattack once our own line is secure.

dialogue.speaker: Aurél Stromfeld
dialogue.role: Chief of Staff, Hungarian Red Army
dialogue.text: Feed the reserve over only while we can protect the crossing. If the bridge comes under fire, stop the next unit. We need a way to bring the leading formations back.

dialogue.speaker: Vilmos Böhm
dialogue.text: At Szolnok we stop improvising. Hold the bridge, depots and command post. Every battalion must know where its ammunition comes from and where the reserve waits.

orders.situation: Romanian forces have reached the Tisza, and an advance detachment has crossed at Szolnok. Hungarian formations are exhausted but now possess a defensible river line.
orders.mission: Secure the western bank, contain the Romanian bridgehead, and establish a viable defensive position around Szolnok.
primaryObjectives: Hold at least four victory objectives
secondaryObjectives: Prevent the Romanian vanguard from expanding its bridgehead
Establish a bridgehead on the eastern bank only when the western defence is secure
orders.enemyIntelligence: Romanian reinforcements will continue to arrive. The first crossing force is smaller than the formations moving toward the battlefield.
orders.availableSupport: An ammunition-wagon detachment is assigned. Two new units may be purchased, and four free RTP slots are available.
orders.notes: 14 turns. The defence of the west bank takes priority over an unsupported advance east of the Tisza.

intro:
Defending Salgótarján

May 9, 1919

Comrade Commisar, while your troops defended Szolnok, the Czech henchmen of the capitalist warlords took Miskolc, the biggest industrial center in North-East Hungary. Now they are surrounding Salgótarján, the last city with steal factory and strong organized working class outside of Budapest. You should relieve Salgótarján immediately!

ORDER: Hold at least 2 VHs and keep your MSU alive.

NOTES:
- You can purchase three new units.
- You have 4 free RTP slots.

15 Turns

Scenario designed by Csaba (lvjtn)

lose.text: The front has collapsed. The Republic has lost the army and time it needed; hostile forces advance while counterrevolutionary detachments prepare their reprisals.

dialogue.speaker: János Kovács
dialogue.text: The eastern front held, and the factories heard about it. Salgotarjan's workers are arming themselves without waiting for authorisation.

dialogue.speaker: János Kovács
dialogue.text: The front held at a price the industry cannot pay twice. Salgotarjan's output is already falling.

dialogue.speaker: János Kovács
dialogue.text: The front has held. Now the miners want to know whether the army is coming to Salgótarján. I need an answer before I go back to the union office.

dialogue.speaker: Gyula Hevesi
dialogue.text: Szolnok is held. The Romanians must now force a river crossing under our guns instead of walking across it.

dialogue.speaker: Gyula Hevesi
dialogue.text: The military base at Szolnok fell to us with its stores largely intact. The People's Commissariat has stopped rationing small-arms ammunition.

dialogue.speaker: Béla Szántó
dialogue.text: I feared keeping the reserve west would cost us the initiative. It recovered the base and its ammunition. I'll support you if the Council questions the decision.

dialogue.speaker: Aurél Stromfeld
dialogue.role: Chief of Staff, Hungarian Red Army
dialogue.text: The stores were lost before I released the reserve. You followed my advice in holding it west. I'll explain that to the supply officers myself.

dialogue.speaker: Aurél Stromfeld
dialogue.role: Chief of Staff, Hungarian Red Army
dialogue.text: You sent the reserve east and the bridgehead held. Böhm called it enthusiasm outrunning supply; the result forced the Romanian staff to treat the Tisza as a front instead of a finish line.

dialogue.speaker: Gyula Hevesi
dialogue.text: The bridgehead didn't hold. Those battalions won't be on the relief trains. What can I tell the miners we're sending instead?

dialogue.speaker: Gyula Hevesi
dialogue.text: You kept much of the army's equipment in the last operation. I need some of it sent into Salgótarján. The workers are afraid the field formations will stay outside while their streets are attacked.

dialogue.speaker: János Kovács
dialogue.text: The men came straight from the pits to the union office for rifles. Some still had their lamps on. I've kept them at the barricades, but that means the furnace crews aren't working. How long must we hold like this?

dialogue.speaker: Gyula Hevesi
dialogue.text: Salgótarján supplies the coal, steel and railway repairs we need for the next offensive. Its workers have armed themselves. If we leave them without help, I won't get another industrial town to trust our promises.

dialogue.speaker: Aurél Stromfeld
dialogue.role: Chief of Staff, Hungarian Red Army
dialogue.text: The Czechoslovak columns are closing from three directions. March straight in and we may trap our relief force beside the miners. Break the Kisterenye pincer first, or push gunners and ammunition through now?

choices.text: Concentrate against Kisterenye and break one arm of the encirclement before reinforcing the city.
choices.hint: Gain a prestige award and substantial experience for every core formation, but forgo the two worker battalions.

choices.text: Push supplies and cadres directly into Salgótarján; the workers must hold while the field units counterattack outside.
choices.hint: Raise two worker battalions and earn their later support, but pay prestige and forgo the core-wide experience award.

dialogue.speaker: Aurél Stromfeld
dialogue.role: Chief of Staff, Hungarian Red Army
dialogue.text: Break the nearest pincer and keep the road open. Kovács will have to hold without us for those hours. I will put that promise in writing before his battalion returns to the barricades.

dialogue.speaker: Gyula Hevesi
dialogue.text: The miners will hold the furnaces and railway yards, but they need trained gunners and ammunition more than speeches. Get those through, and they will give you the time to strike outside the city.

dialogue.speaker: János Kovács
dialogue.text: We can guide you through the cuttings and slag heaps. Some of our companies are still in pit clothes, but they know the ground. What we haven't got is enough trained men for the guns from the depot.

dialogue.speaker: Aurél Stromfeld
dialogue.role: Chief of Staff, Hungarian Red Army
dialogue.text: Kovács, mark the road from the pits to our guns. Commissar, get it open before his ammunition runs out. Then we can assemble the counterattack at the railway yard.

orders.situation: Czechoslovak forces have taken Miskolc and are attempting to surround Salgótarján from several directions. Local miners and factory workers are mobilising to defend the industrial district.
orders.mission: Relieve Salgótarján, break the developing encirclement, and keep the industrial and railway centres in revolutionary hands.
primaryObjectives: Hold at least two victory objectives
secondaryObjectives: Keep at least one route into Salgótarján open
Preserve the worker formations and industrial objectives
orders.enemyIntelligence: Enemy columns are advancing toward the Salgótarján basin from multiple directions. Their success depends on completing the encirclement before relief forces concentrate.
orders.availableSupport: Three new units may be purchased. Four free RTP slots are available. Local worker companies can strengthen the urban defence.
orders.notes: 15 turns. Prevent the relief force and city garrison from being defeated separately.

intro:
Liberating Miskolc

May 23, 1919

Comrade Commisar, tens of thousands proletars joined the Hungarian Red Army. These factory workers are eager to fight against the capitalist marauders and their mercenaries. Though our new red soldiers aren't trained well enough to defeat the Romanians, we are ready to push back the Czechs, who are famous for their low commitment to fight. Comrade, let's liberate Miskolc!

ORDER: Take all VHs and keep your MSU alive.

NOTES:
- You can purchase two new units.
- You have 5 free RTP slots.

20 Turns

Scenario designed by Csaba (lvjtn)

lose.text: The front has collapsed. The Republic has lost the army and time it needed; hostile forces advance while counterrevolutionary detachments prepare their reprisals.

dialogue.speaker: Gyula Hevesi
dialogue.text: Salgótarján is intact. The Czechoslovak command has lost time recovering, so we can prepare the northern operation. Tell me what the factories must supply first.

dialogue.speaker: Gyula Hevesi
dialogue.text: We have the mines. The formations need rest and replacements before we send them north. I can promise production; I can't promise those men another battle yet.

dialogue.speaker: Gyula Hevesi
dialogue.text: The industrial district is held. We may go north - carefully, and with the supply columns kept close behind the mobile formations.

dialogue.speaker: Aurél Stromfeld
dialogue.role: Chief of Staff, Hungarian Red Army
dialogue.text: The northern industrial belt held completely. Salgotarjan is still producing, and what it produces is reaching the front.

dialogue.speaker: Aurél Stromfeld
dialogue.role: Chief of Staff, Hungarian Red Army
dialogue.text: We saved part of the industrial district. The output is a fraction of what it was, and the miners know exactly which pits we could not defend.

dialogue.speaker: János Kovács
dialogue.text: You sent us men who could train the companies. They held. The furnaces are working again, and the crews want me to tell you they remember the rifles arriving.

dialogue.speaker: János Kovács
dialogue.text: We took the rifles and held as long as we could. Some pits won't reopen. Before you thank us, tell me why the relief came after the furnaces went cold.

dialogue.speaker: Aurél Stromfeld
dialogue.role: Chief of Staff, Hungarian Red Army
dialogue.text: You backed my attack on the Kisterenye pincer. The road opened and the industrial belt held. Kovács still had to fight alone while we did it. I'll hear him out if he has a complaint.

dialogue.speaker: János Kovács
dialogue.text: You broke the pincer. We couldn't hold all the city until you arrived. Come and look at the pits we've lost before you tell the men the manoeuvre was necessary.

dialogue.speaker: Gyula Hevesi
dialogue.text: Salgótarján is sending shells north and bringing wounded men back. Miskolc's workshops and junction are next. Can you take them without cutting the line we need to supply you?

dialogue.speaker: Aurél Stromfeld
dialogue.role: Chief of Staff, Hungarian Red Army
dialogue.text: Miskolc would give us the northern railway and workshops. I want them taken, but I also want formations left for the advance afterward. Landler, which approach costs us least?

dialogue.speaker: Jenő Landler
dialogue.text: The garrison covers several approaches and will counterattack the moment one quarter falls. How do we take the city without feeding the new worker battalions into prepared streets—turn the position by cutting its northern roads, or strike every entrance before the defenders can concentrate?

choices.text: Fix the defenders in front while mobile units cut the northern roads and force an evacuation.
choices.hint: Gain a prestige award and experience for every core reconnaissance unit, but forgo the artillery detachment and near-full resupply.

choices.text: Attack from several directions at once, seize the stations, and prevent the garrison from concentrating.
choices.hint: Gain a mountain-artillery detachment and near-full core resupply, but forgo the turning attack's prestige and reconnaissance experience.

dialogue.speaker: Aurél Stromfeld
dialogue.role: Chief of Staff, Hungarian Red Army
dialogue.text: Use the mobile force to threaten their communications. Keep pressure in front so the garrison cannot all turn against it. Report when the northern road is cut.

dialogue.speaker: Gyula Hevesi
dialogue.text: If the turning column stalls, the new worker battalions will face the garrison alone. I accept the order. I also want a time on the map when those battalions stop waiting and pull back.

dialogue.speaker: Jenő Landler
dialogue.text: Then the attacks must be simultaneous. A piecemeal assault will feed inexperienced battalions into prepared positions one after another.

dialogue.speaker: Aurél Stromfeld
dialogue.role: Chief of Staff, Hungarian Red Army
dialogue.text: I'll write the timings. But a broken telephone could leave one column attacking alone. Every commander needs instructions for that before we begin, Landler.

dialogue.speaker: Gyula Hevesi
dialogue.text: The furnaces are still hot. Keep shellfire out of the works if you can, and leave men at the stations after they fall. I need a city that can repair this army tomorrow.

dialogue.speaker: Aurél Stromfeld
dialogue.role: Chief of Staff, Hungarian Red Army
dialogue.text: Take Miskolc without letting the garrison consume the attacking force. I want the command group and the northern road ready when Kassa becomes the next order.

orders.situation: Mass mobilisation has rebuilt the Hungarian Red Army. Miskolc, an important industrial and railway centre, is held by Czechoslovak forces supported by nearby Romanian formations.
orders.mission: Retake Miskolc, destroy or dislodge the defending force, and secure the base for the Northern Campaign.
secondaryObjectives: Secure the railway junctions and industrial districts intact
Retain enough combat power to defeat the expected counterattack
orders.enemyIntelligence: The enemy recognises Miskolc as both a political and strategic objective. Expect a concentrated defence followed by an attempt to retake the city.
orders.availableSupport: Two new units may be purchased. Five free RTP slots are available. Newly mobilised worker battalions expand the available force.
orders.notes: 20 turns. Do not disperse the assault force among minor targets before the railway and city objectives are secure.

intro:
Liberating Kassa (Koice)

May 30, 1919

Comrade Commisar, our offensive is going well, and our soldiers are eager to take a revenge for previous losses, another shiny victory would boost their morale. More importantly, there is a good opportunity to deliver a severe blow to the Czech marauders. Comrade, your job is to liberate Kassa with its important steel industry and railways junctions.

ORDER: Take all VHs and keep your MSU alive.

NOTES:
- You can purchase two new units.
- You have 5 free RTP slots.

18 Turns

Scenario designed by Csaba (lvjtn)

lose.text: The front has collapsed. The Republic has lost the army and time it needed; hostile forces advance while counterrevolutionary detachments prepare their reprisals.

dialogue.speaker: Mária Tóth
dialogue.text: Miskolc fell before their staff could reinforce it. The northern grouping is losing its supply links. My crews want to know when we're moving again.

dialogue.speaker: Mária Tóth
dialogue.text: I have the Miskolc transport returns. The corps needs replacements before we ask it to pursue. Shall I put those trains ahead of the artillery?

dialogue.speaker: Mária Tóth
dialogue.text: Miskolc is ours. The advance can continue, though the mobile formations have already outrun their columns.

dialogue.speaker: Jenő Landler
dialogue.text: Ozd and Kazincbarcika came through undamaged. The furnaces are lit, the rolling mills are turning, and the railway repair shops are ours.

dialogue.speaker: Jenő Landler
dialogue.text: We took Miskolc and lost the works at Ozd and Kazincbarcika doing it. What we need now cannot be manufactured behind this front.

dialogue.speaker: Jenő Landler
dialogue.text: Miskolc is secure and the northern road is open.

dialogue.speaker: Gyula Hevesi
dialogue.text: I was worried your turning column would stall. It opened the road and the works survived. Bring me the next route plan early; I'll help with the transport before we argue over it.

dialogue.speaker: Gyula Hevesi
dialogue.text: The mobile columns got their road. Ózd and Kazincbarcika lost their works. I need you to explain why the industrial flank was left exposed; the workers won't accept an answer from me.

dialogue.speaker: Jenő Landler
dialogue.text: You gave Stromfeld time to coordinate the assaults I wanted. The stations fell together and the works survived. Next time I'm pressing him to hurry, you have my permission to mention Miskolc.

dialogue.speaker: Aurél Stromfeld
dialogue.role: Chief of Staff, Hungarian Red Army
dialogue.text: I set the attack hours. The columns still lost contact and the works burned while they waited. Keep my timetable with the reports. I need to find out which orders failed to reach them.

dialogue.speaker: Mária Tóth
dialogue.text: My old crew is still inside Kassa. They smuggled out this timetable with three grease marks for trains the garrison has not filled yet. Give them our signal, and they will lock those engines in the sheds.

dialogue.speaker: Jenő Landler
dialogue.text: A month ago we could barely find headquarters for these formations. Now they're arguing over who leads. Kassa's junction is the next objective. Can we reach it before the enemy brings its fronts together?

dialogue.speaker: Aurél Stromfeld
dialogue.role: Chief of Staff, Hungarian Red Army
dialogue.text: The line is shaken, but our spearheads have already outrun repaired track. Do we pursue before Kassa can organise, accepting thin supply, or pause just long enough to bring artillery and railway crews forward for a battle we can sustain after the first day?

choices.text: Advance at once. Deny the enemy time to organise Kassa and seize the junction before reinforcements arrive.
choices.hint: Gain a larger prestige award and experience for every core formation, but forgo the armoured train and full resupply.

choices.text: Bring up artillery, repair the railway, and strike with the divisions supplied for a sustained battle.
choices.hint: Gain an armoured train and fully resupply every core formation, but forgo the rapid pursuit's prestige and core-wide experience.

dialogue.speaker: Jenő Landler
dialogue.text: Keep the spearhead concentrated. Leave guards at the stations and pass scattered resistance to the following units. Send me word if anything actually blocks the main road.

dialogue.speaker: Aurél Stromfeld
dialogue.role: Chief of Staff, Hungarian Red Army
dialogue.text: Bring up the guns and repair the track. I want progress reports by the hour. We cannot let a short pause become several days for the Kassa garrison to prepare.

dialogue.speaker: Mária Tóth
dialogue.text: My contacts say the Kassa switches and sheds are intact. Put engineers with the leading infantry. The crews can help us use the junction if demolition parties don't get there first.

dialogue.speaker: Aurél Stromfeld
dialogue.role: Chief of Staff, Hungarian Red Army
dialogue.text: Then the engineers go forward. Tóth, pass the signal to your crews. I need those locomotives available when the first units reach Kassa.

orders.situation: The recapture of Miskolc has opened the Northern Campaign. Czechoslovak forces are withdrawing toward Kassa, but they still control the principal railway junctions and industrial objectives.
orders.mission: Seize Kassa before the enemy can stabilise the front, and preserve the transport network for the continued advance.
secondaryObjectives: Capture the railway facilities intact
Prevent enemy forces from forming a new continuous defensive line
orders.enemyIntelligence: The defeated formations are falling back on prepared communications. Reinforcements may arrive if the advance loses momentum.
orders.availableSupport: Two new units may be purchased. Five free RTP slots are available. Railway workers may assist once the junction is secured.
orders.notes: 18 turns. Balance operational speed with the need to keep the spearhead supplied.

intro:
Bártfa (Bardejov): Reaching The Polish Border

June 9, 1919

Comrade Commisar, the Czech capitalists are in disarray, they didn't expect how strong the Red Army of workers and peasants could be when they get a proper training about the dialectical materialism. Now we have a unique chance to cut off the Czech defense lines and separate the Romanian and Czech invaders once and for all. Let the Iron Fist of the factory workers smash these imperialist bandits! Your order is to liberate Bártfa near the Polish border.

ORDER: Take all VHs and keep your MSU alive.

NOTES:
- You can purchase two new units.
- You have 5 free RTP slots.

20 Turns

Scenario designed by Csaba (lvjtn)

lose.text: The front has collapsed. The Republic has lost the army and time it needed; hostile forces advance while counterrevolutionary detachments prepare their reprisals.

briefing.act: ACT VII — TO THE POLISH BORDER

dialogue.speaker: Antonín Janoušek
dialogue.text: The Kassa presses are sending Slovak appeals north. My organisers are already talking about a republic. I need to know which committees can actually meet before I let them put names on a proclamation.

dialogue.speaker: Antonín Janoušek
dialogue.text: We've taken Kassa, but the road to Eperjes is still a problem. I can't send organisers up it on the strength of a leaflet. When can your columns go through?

dialogue.speaker: Antonín Janoušek
dialogue.text: The appeals are going north from Kassa and committees are forming. Several want to speak for the new republic. I have to get them into the same room before one announces it alone.

dialogue.speaker: Aurél Stromfeld
dialogue.role: Chief of Staff, Hungarian Red Army
dialogue.text: Kassa is ours, and the junction with it. Every train the Czechoslovak command wanted to move south now goes the long way or not at all.

dialogue.speaker: Aurél Stromfeld
dialogue.role: Chief of Staff, Hungarian Red Army
dialogue.text: The Kassa pursuit got ahead of the repaired supply line. I have commanders asking to go farther and trains that can't reach them. Set the limit before I issue another movement order.

dialogue.speaker: Jenő Landler
dialogue.text: We waited for Stromfeld's guns and railway crews at Kassa. He has supplied divisions now. I still think we gave the enemy useful hours; we'll see what they've done with them at the next position.

dialogue.speaker: Antonín Janoušek
dialogue.text: Before we print another appeal, read this question from Eperjes: will their councils govern, or will Budapest? I need an answer I can give the organisers. They're watching what our battalions do.

dialogue.speaker: Aurél Stromfeld
dialogue.role: Chief of Staff, Hungarian Red Army
dialogue.text: Bártfa would cut across the separating enemy fronts, near the Polish border. Supply gets difficult that far north. I need the ammunition route agreed, and someone speaking to the villages along it.

dialogue.speaker: Antonín Janoušek
dialogue.text: Workers in the occupied towns ask whether the Red Army has come to restore old Hungarian rule or to help them elect councils of their own. Forbid undisciplined requisition, publish orders in the local languages, and make the answer visible before nationalist officers provide one of their own.

dialogue.speaker: Jenő Landler
dialogue.text: Some of these soldiers want Kassa back in Hungary. They haven't marched north to create a separate state. Tell them what you're proposing before you ask them to defend it.

dialogue.speaker: Antonín Janoušek
dialogue.text: Then help me tell them. We can't ask Slovak workers to reject Prague and accept orders from Budapest instead. Their councils must have authority of their own, or they won't trust us.

dialogue.speaker: Jenő Landler
dialogue.text: The columns still need a route. Keep them on the railway where we can supply and control them, or send them through parallel valleys so one roadblock can't hold everyone? Commissar?

choices.text: Drive the main force along the railway and seize each junction before the enemy can demolish it.
choices.hint: Gain a transport column, a larger prestige award and near-full core resupply, but forgo the parallel advance's core-wide experience.

choices.text: Advance in parallel columns through the valleys so one roadblock cannot halt the whole operation.
choices.hint: Gain a prestige award and experience for every core formation, but forgo the transport column and near-full resupply.

dialogue.speaker: Aurél Stromfeld
dialogue.role: Chief of Staff, Hungarian Red Army
dialogue.text: The railway gives speed and supply, but it also makes our intention obvious. Keep flank detachments on the heights and engineers at the head of the column.

dialogue.speaker: Jenő Landler
dialogue.text: Give the columns meeting points and keep them within supporting distance. If one is stopped, the others need to know before they move beyond it.

dialogue.speaker: Antonín Janoušek
dialogue.text: I'll send organisers behind the columns. Have the commanders enforce receipts for requisitions and leave elected councils in the villages. I can't persuade people to trust us if the next battalion ignores their decisions.

orders.situation: The Northern Campaign has carried the Red Army deep into Upper Hungary. Czechoslovak forces are disorganised, but the army is operating far from its main depots in difficult terrain.
orders.mission: Seize Bártfa, disrupt the enemy communications near the Polish border, and preserve the cohesion of the northern advance.
secondaryObjectives: Keep the advancing columns mutually supporting
Protect the railway and road network needed for supply
orders.enemyIntelligence: The enemy is retreating but can exploit mountain roads, demolitions, and local counterattacks to isolate the spearheads.
orders.availableSupport: Two new units may be purchased. Five free RTP slots are available. Local revolutionary organisers can help establish administration behind the front.
orders.notes: 20 turns. The operational goal is to split the enemy fronts, not to scatter the army in pursuit of every retreating unit.

intro:
Defending Érsekújvár (Nové Zámky)

June 13, 1919

Ah, dear Comrade Commisar, have you got the dedicated copy of Lenin's The State and Revolution? Comrade Szamuely has just arrived from Moscow with the warmest greetings and this special present for you. Our international revolution is going well, our Slovakian comrades will declare their Soviet Republic within days. Unfortunately these pesky Czech marauders simply can't accept their defeat, and they launched a strong counterattack in the area of Nyitra (Nitra) - Vág (Váh) - Garam (Hron) rivers. Give these imperialist lapdogs a bloody nose again!

ORDER: Hold at least 3 VHs and keep your MSU alive.

NOTES:
- You can repurchase only the lost units.
- Both sides get valuable reinforcements.
- You have 5 free RTP slots.

20 Turns

Scenario designed by Csaba (lvjtn)

lose.text: The front has collapsed. The Republic has lost the army and time it needed; hostile forces advance while counterrevolutionary detachments prepare their reprisals.

dialogue.speaker: Béla Kun
dialogue.text: The northern operation has succeeded beyond anything the Entente allowed for. That success is precisely why Clemenceau's note arrived this morning.

dialogue.speaker: Béla Kun
dialogue.text: The advance has stalled, and the note from Paris is timed to exploit exactly that.

dialogue.speaker: Béla Kun
dialogue.text: The north is held. And now Paris sends us a map with our borders already drawn upon it.

dialogue.speaker: Tibor Szamuely
dialogue.text: The Eperjes delegates are preparing their proclamation. They're still arguing over who signs it. If we accept the withdrawal Paris demands, what am I supposed to tell them?

dialogue.speaker: Tibor Szamuely
dialogue.text: Bartfa, Eperjes, Golnicbanya - the whole northern axis. No staff in Europe expected this army to be standing here in June.

dialogue.speaker: Mária Tóth
dialogue.text: I wrote the ammunition trains over Fekete's old evacuation timetable. This time the loaded wagons went north and the wounded came back on schedule. The crews no longer ask whether your orders understand a railway.

dialogue.speaker: Antonín Janoušek
dialogue.text: Several villages elected councils before the main force reached them. Then they received requisition orders from three columns. Please settle who may issue those orders before I send more organisers.

dialogue.speaker: Béla Kun
dialogue.text: Here is Clemenceau's note. It offers a frontier and Romanian withdrawal if we leave the north. I have no Romanian withdrawal order to set beside it. They are already demanding that we begin ours.

dialogue.speaker: Tibor Szamuely
dialogue.text: Moscow sent greetings. No army is coming over the Carpathians with them. The men and Slovak workers holding the north are the help we have. Why give up their ground before Romania moves?

dialogue.speaker: Béla Kun
dialogue.text: Because rejecting the note gives Paris a reason to back every neighbouring army against us. How long can we fight all of them? I don't trust the promise either, but I have to consider accepting it.

dialogue.speaker: Aurél Stromfeld
dialogue.role: Chief of Staff, Hungarian Red Army
dialogue.text: Take your hands off my map, both of you. Budapest may bargain over the north; the Czechoslovak columns are already moving through it. Commissar, give this front an order it can obey tonight.

dialogue.speaker: Béla Kun
dialogue.text: The Czechoslovak columns are attacking between Nyitra, the Vág and the Garam. Do we hold the crossings and use depth, or concentrate at once and break the strongest column before diplomacy becomes a military fact?

choices.text: Hold the river crossings and trade exposed ground for time until our reinforcements arrive.
choices.hint: Fully resupply every core formation and gain an entrenched infantry detachment, but forgo the counterattack's prestige and core-wide experience.

choices.text: Concentrate immediately against the strongest enemy column and break the offensive before it develops.
choices.hint: Gain a prestige award and experience for every core formation, but forgo full resupply and the additional infantry detachment.

dialogue.speaker: Aurél Stromfeld
dialogue.role: Chief of Staff, Hungarian Red Army
dialogue.text: An elastic defence is sound only if the crossings remain organised. Mark the line beyond which no unit withdraws without orders, or controlled movement will become retreat.

dialogue.speaker: Aurél Stromfeld
dialogue.role: Chief of Staff, Hungarian Red Army
dialogue.text: Then I want the artillery massed before the infantry moves. Strike one column while it is still alone. If eager battalions go early, they will warn the enemy and spend our advantage.

dialogue.speaker: Tibor Szamuely
dialogue.text: The soldiers have heard we're negotiating the ground away. Give them a definite order for tonight. I can go to the battalions, but I won't promise them that Paris has agreed anything.

dialogue.speaker: Aurél Stromfeld
dialogue.role: Chief of Staff, Hungarian Red Army
dialogue.text: Keep the three crossings under one command. Counterattack when the enemy columns separate. Send political instructions through headquarters; I won't have battalions changing position on rumours of a settlement.

orders.situation: The Red Army has reached the high point of the Northern Campaign, but Czechoslovak forces are counterattacking along the Nyitra–Vág–Garam sector while Entente diplomatic pressure increases.
orders.mission: Hold the Érsekújvár sector, defeat the enemy counterattack, and prevent the northern front from being cut away from Hungary.
primaryObjectives: Hold at least three victory objectives
secondaryObjectives: Preserve the river crossings and the connection between defending formations
Counterattack once the enemy offensive loses momentum
orders.enemyIntelligence: The Czechoslovak command has committed a strong counterattack. Both sides will receive valuable reinforcements during the battle.
orders.availableSupport: Lost units may be repurchased, but no additional formations beyond replacements are authorised. Five free RTP slots are available.
orders.notes: 20 turns. Political uncertainty must not be allowed to disrupt the local chain of command.

intro:
Szolnok-Mezöhegyes Offensive

July 19, 1919

The imperialists fooled us. They promised the Romanian troops would withdraw behind the demarcation line declared on March 20 in exchange for our withdrawal from the Fölvidék (Upper Hungary). But the enemies of our communist revolution broke their words, and their Romanian mercenaries are still staying behind the Tisza. It's time to teach these truce-breakers a hard lesson and liberate our proletarian sisters and brothers by force! Lead our troops to victory, Comrade Commisar!

ORDER: Take all VHs and keep your MSU alive.

NOTES:
- You can repurchase only the lost units.
- AI gets valuable reinforcements.
- You have 6 free RTP slots.

20 Turns

Scenario designed by Csaba (lvjtn)

lose.text: The front has collapsed. The Republic has lost the army and time it needed; hostile forces advance while counterrevolutionary detachments prepare their reprisals.

dialogue.speaker: Ferenc Julier
dialogue.role: Chief of Staff, Hungarian Red Army
dialogue.text: Comrade, this army withdrew from Slovakia undefeated. Whatever the government has promised Paris, the formations that crossed back are still capable of an offensive.

dialogue.speaker: Ferenc Julier
dialogue.role: Chief of Staff, Hungarian Red Army
dialogue.text: We gave up Slovakia and gained nothing for it. Stromfeld resigned rather than sign the order, and the staff has not recovered from it.

dialogue.speaker: Ferenc Julier
dialogue.role: Chief of Staff, Hungarian Red Army
dialogue.text: The north has been evacuated. I have the formations, but their officers want to know why they should trust the next government order. I can't ignore that before an offensive.

dialogue.speaker: Jenő Landler
dialogue.text: We held the mining towns to the end and then evacuated them under orders, not under fire. The men have not forgotten the difference.

dialogue.speaker: Jenő Landler
dialogue.text: Your elastic defence kept the crossings organised and brought formations back. We can use them again. They'll want to hear why this offensive will be different from the victorious ground we just gave up.

dialogue.speaker: Jenő Landler
dialogue.text: The men who counterattacked at Érsekújvár know they weren't driven out of Slovakia. They're angry about withdrawing anyway. The new staff also needs ammunition and replacements for what that attack cost.

dialogue.speaker: Ferenc Julier
dialogue.role: Chief of Staff, Hungarian Red Army
dialogue.text: They've taken Stromfeld's chair out. His pencil marks are still on the maps. When I ask for a report, the officers look at that space first. I need them to work with me, Landler, whether they approve of the withdrawal or not.

dialogue.speaker: Jenő Landler
dialogue.text: Paris promised the Romanians would leave. They haven't. Stromfeld resigned, and now every order gets questioned. We still have formations that can fight. You need to tell their officers what we're asking before distrust makes the decision for us.

dialogue.speaker: Ferenc Julier
dialogue.role: Chief of Staff, Hungarian Red Army
dialogue.text: We cross at several points, with the main effort at Szolnok. The pontoons cannot carry everyone, and Romania expects us. Does the strongest reserve follow that bridgehead at once, or wait centrally for a crossing that proves it can live?

choices.text: Commit it behind the Szolnok bridgehead and drive deep before the Romanian command can concentrate.
choices.hint: Gain a prestige award and experience for every core formation, but forgo full resupply and the experienced International Brigade.

choices.text: Hold the reserve centrally and reinforce whichever crossing gains a secure bridgehead first.
choices.hint: Fully resupply every core formation and gain an experienced International Brigade, but forgo the deep thrust's prestige and core-wide experience.

dialogue.speaker: Jenő Landler
dialogue.text: Send engineers, guns and supplies directly after the assault. If the main bridgehead moves quickly, Romania will have to concentrate against it. Don't let the leading divisions get beyond what the bridge can supply.

dialogue.speaker: Ferenc Julier
dialogue.role: Chief of Staff, Hungarian Red Army
dialogue.text: Once it crosses, I have no fresh reserve for a counterattack. I'll send it, Landler. But if the bridgehead stalls, don't ask me for a formation I've already committed.

dialogue.speaker: Ferenc Julier
dialogue.role: Chief of Staff, Hungarian Red Army
dialogue.text: Set the conditions for releasing it now. Otherwise every crossing will call for help and the reserve will spend the battle changing roads.

dialogue.speaker: Jenő Landler
dialogue.text: Give one commander authority to release it. If we wait for every crossing report to agree, the successful bridgehead may have stopped advancing by the time help arrives.

dialogue.speaker: Béla Kun
dialogue.text: If this fails, Budapest is exposed. I need an army Bucharest and Paris have to reckon with. Tell the soldiers what the crossing requires, not that victory will be easy.

dialogue.speaker: Ferenc Julier
dialogue.role: Chief of Staff, Hungarian Red Army
dialogue.text: Get the first guns over before surprise is gone. Widen only the bridgeheads you can feed, and keep headquarters close enough to know which bridges still exist.

orders.situation: The Red Army has withdrawn from the Northern Campaign, while Romanian troops remain east of the Tisza. A general Hungarian offensive is prepared along the river, with the main effort centred on Szolnok.
orders.mission: Force the Tisza, expand the bridgeheads, and defeat the Romanian forces before their numerical superiority can be concentrated.
secondaryObjectives: Protect the crossing sites and supply routes
Exploit success without allowing the assault divisions to outrun artillery and ammunition
orders.enemyIntelligence: Romanian intelligence anticipates a major attack and valuable reinforcements are available to the defending army.
orders.availableSupport: Only lost units may be repurchased. Six free RTP slots are available.
orders.notes: 20 turns. The historical offensive began at dawn on 20 July; the scenario date represents the final deployment and opening movement.

intro:
Szolnok: The Collapse

July 24, 1919

Comrade Commisar, the situation is critical. Though we have managed to cross Tisza at three locations, and we have gained a large bridgehead east of Szolnok, our offensive has stalled. Our soldiers are exhausted, we have serious difficulties to resupply them, while more and more fresh Romanian troops are arriving at the battlefields. We suspects some of the former KuK officiers in our rank have betrayed our Soviet Republic and delivered important intels to the imperialists. Comrade, a strong and overwhelming capitalist counterattack is imminent! Save our revolution and do not let them cross the Tisza!

ORDER: Hold at least three VHs and keep your MSU alive.

NOTES:
- AI moves first.
- You can repurchase only the lost units.
- AI gets valuable reinforcements.
- You have 4 free RTP slots.

20 Turns

Scenario designed by Csaba (lvjtn)

briliant.text: The Romanian counterattack failed to destroy the Szolnok command before the battle ended. The surviving formations still answered orders, but one sector could not reverse the collapse around it. Over the following week the wider front gave way; on 1 August the Revolutionary Governing Council resigned. Your last decision did not decide whether the Republic survived—it decided what survived it.

victory.text: The Szolnok front survived the first blow and denied the Romanian command an immediate decision. It bought the Republic days, not a reversal. As the wider front disintegrated, the Revolutionary Governing Council resigned on 1 August. What remained under discipline at Szolnok became part of the Republic's legacy rather than its rescue.

tactical.text: Szolnok did not become an immediate rout, but the battle ended without a force capable of restoring the offensive. Romanian troops broke the wider front in the following days, and on 1 August the Revolutionary Governing Council resigned. The Republic fell; the people and formations preserved here still had to survive its defeat.

lose.text: The Szolnok front collapsed under the Romanian counterattack. Disintegration spread faster than orders could contain it; on 1 August the Revolutionary Governing Council resigned. With organised resistance shattered, counterrevolutionary forces began settling political accounts against an increasingly defenceless enemy.

dialogue.speaker: Ferenc Julier
dialogue.role: Chief of Staff, Hungarian Red Army
dialogue.text: The Tisza crossing succeeded. I will not pretend the staff expected it - the Romanian command certainly did not.

dialogue.speaker: Ferenc Julier
dialogue.role: Chief of Staff, Hungarian Red Army
dialogue.text: The offensive has stopped on the far bank. I need fresh orders for the formations there before the Romanian counterattack reaches them.

dialogue.speaker: Ferenc Julier
dialogue.role: Chief of Staff, Hungarian Red Army
dialogue.text: We hold a bridgehead. Whether it can be supplied across a river under observed artillery is the only question that now matters.

dialogue.speaker: Ferenc Julier
dialogue.role: Chief of Staff, Hungarian Red Army
dialogue.text: The army survived the evacuation from Slovakia and has crossed the Tisza. That gives us a chance Paris and Bucharest didn't expect. It doesn't give us much time to repair this position.

dialogue.speaker: Ferenc Julier
dialogue.role: Chief of Staff, Hungarian Red Army
dialogue.text: The advance went beyond Szolnok, farther than we planned. Check those leading formations first. I need to know which roads they can use coming back.

dialogue.speaker: Ferenc Julier
dialogue.role: Chief of Staff, Hungarian Red Army
dialogue.text: We hold a bridgehead and no more. The crossing succeeded; the exploitation did not.

dialogue.speaker: Ferenc Julier
dialogue.role: Chief of Staff, Hungarian Red Army
dialogue.text: We committed the reserve deep, as you ordered. There is nothing left behind the line to commit again.

dialogue.speaker: Ferenc Julier
dialogue.role: Chief of Staff, Hungarian Red Army
dialogue.text: The central reserve is still available. Landler wanted it across sooner; now he's asking where we'll commit it. I need that decision before the next crossing report arrives.

dialogue.speaker: Ferenc Julier
dialogue.role: Chief of Staff, Hungarian Red Army
dialogue.text: Try the east-bank headquarters again. Some telephone lines have been shelled; others reach offices the staff has already left. I can't place the divisions from these reports. Send runners along the roads we still hold.

dialogue.speaker: Ferenc Julier
dialogue.role: Chief of Staff, Hungarian Red Army
dialogue.text: The divisions east of Szolnok are exhausted. Ammunition isn't crossing fast enough, and Romanian formations are gathering for a counterattack. We have to shorten the position or begin moving units back.

dialogue.speaker: Jenő Landler
dialogue.text: Some reports say the Romanians knew our advance routes. We can investigate how later. For now: send the last reserve into the eastern bridgehead, or start withdrawing before they reach the crossings?

choices.text: Hold the eastern bridgehead with every available reserve and deny the enemy the initiative.
choices.hint: Gain a larger prestige award and experience for every core formation, but forgo the withdrawal's full resupply.

choices.text: Withdraw the most exhausted units first and build a final defence around the crossings on the west bank.
choices.hint: Fully resupply every core formation and gain a smaller prestige award, but forgo the final stand's core-wide experience.

dialogue.speaker: Ferenc Julier
dialogue.role: Chief of Staff, Hungarian Red Army
dialogue.text: Then shorten the perimeter and mass the guns. Do not defend empty ground. The bridgehead survives only if its flanks and the bridge itself remain under one command.

dialogue.speaker: Jenő Landler
dialogue.text: I'll pass the order. Tell me how the shortened bridgehead will be supplied. The reserve cannot hold it for long if we can't get ammunition across.

dialogue.speaker: Jenő Landler
dialogue.text: A withdrawal may save the army, but it must begin before the enemy reaches the bridges. Mark the order of movement now and leave disciplined rear guards, not abandoned battalions.

dialogue.speaker: Ferenc Julier
dialogue.role: Chief of Staff, Hungarian Red Army
dialogue.text: After Slovakia, some regiments will hear this as another abandonment. Their officers must receive the movement order before the rumours do. I'll speak to them, but I need the crossing times from you.

dialogue.speaker: Béla Kun
dialogue.text: Budapest is hearing that whole headquarters have disappeared. Foreign missions are waiting for the government to fall. Keep enough of the army together to protect our people if the enemy reaches the capital.

dialogue.speaker: Jenő Landler
dialogue.text: Hold those three points while the fresh Romanian formations come up. The bridges and guns need one command. No counterattack unless it helps us keep the line connected.

orders.situation: The Tisza offensive has stalled east of Szolnok. Hungarian troops are exhausted and undersupplied, while fresh Romanian formations are assembling for a general counterattack.
orders.mission: Prevent the destruction of the bridgehead, preserve the army, and stop Romanian forces from crossing the Tisza toward Budapest.
primaryObjectives: Hold at least three victory objectives
secondaryObjectives: Keep the bridge and withdrawal routes open
Preserve artillery and experienced formations from encirclement
orders.enemyIntelligence: The enemy moves first and receives valuable reinforcements. Assume the Romanian command understands the main Hungarian dispositions and will strike the bridgehead flanks.
orders.availableSupport: Only lost units may be repurchased. Four free RTP slots are available.
orders.notes: 20 turns. Historical suspicions that the plan had been betrayed remain disputed; the briefing therefore treats reconnaissance, interception, and betrayal as alternative explanations.

epilogues.speaker: Ferenc Julier
epilogues.role: Chief of Staff, Hungarian Red Army
epilogues.text: The bridgehead held. For several days I could still issue orders and know where the formations were. It wasn't enough to save the Republic. Landler is speaking to the survivors about their stand. I have to tell them which reserves and guns will not be coming back.

epilogues.speaker: Jenő Landler
epilogues.text: The last reserve was lost with the eastern bridgehead. We had no formed troops here to cover the fugitives. The White Terror is beginning, and men keep asking why we committed their comrades after the position could no longer be held. We owe them an answer.

epilogues.speaker: Béla Kun
epilogues.text: The army crossed back in order. It couldn't keep the Governing Council in power; after 1 August it had no state to defend. Some battalions could still escort threatened comrades and conceal weapons. Find the officers who stayed with them. Those connections may keep people alive.

epilogues.speaker: Ferenc Julier
epilogues.role: Chief of Staff, Hungarian Red Army
epilogues.text: We started too late. Battalions reached the west bank separately, and I couldn't assemble them. With the White Terror beginning, some of those men may still escort or hide comrades. I can no longer promise them organised protection.
